Even though total comparable sales decreased by 2.4%, yet a significant improvement in profitability cheered investors.

"We remain focused on generating long term value for our shareholders and are encouraged by the progress we are making against our strategic plan. These efforts have contributed to improved retail trends and a positive start to the third quarter, giving us confidence in raising our full year guidance,” said CEO Doug Howe. The company also generated double-digit sales growth in its Brand Portfolio segment.
For the second quarter, adjusted EPS stood at $0.34, beating consensus by $0.08, while net sales declined 1% to $730.63, missing estimates by $14.03M.
Cash and cash equivalents totaled $51.6 million at the end of the second quarter of 2026, compared to $44.9 million at the end of the same period last year.
